slides.narration: Chapter 30: The Hardest Test. The cosmic microwave background — the oldest light in the universe — was measured by the Planck satellite at 2,500 data points. The framework reproduces all of them with zero adjustable parameters.

The full CMB power spectrum — temperature, polarization, and their cross-correlation — computed from the framework's parameters, lands within cosmic variance of the Planck measurement at every single data point. The Hubble constant matches to 0.03 standard deviations.

The Hubble constant — the expansion rate of the universe — comes out to 67.38 kilometers per second per megaparsec. Planck measured 67.36. The match is 0.03 standard deviations. This is the framework's most demanding test, and it passes.
